approach: The root cause is at reading acceptance. A reading's deliverables are compared with the base commit's files, but the prose is not. A named earlier job is taken to mean its work landed. Add one pure, model-free `pub fn check_named_dependencies(reading, files, earlier, retried, symbol_found)` in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs beside `check_boundary_and_repo_files`. `read_once` chains it right after `check_reading_acceptance`, so the reader's one correction covers both. Three parts. (1) Path tokens in the reading's prose must be in the snapshot, be a Create deliverable, or be named in out_of_scope. (2) Symbols in `Code survey:` assumptions must be defined or brought into scope by the snapshot's .rs source, be a known external or standard-library item, be marked new, be a create deliverable, or be named in out_of_scope. (3) For earlier jobs, a job's unlanded files (added changed_files and create reading_deliverables absent from the snapshot) count only when the reading's own text names the job id, one of those paths, or a file stem of one. They must then be a Create deliverable or named in out_of_scope. `earlier` is the retried attempt, the jobs the request cites, and now also jobs whose ids appear only in the reading's own text, loaded from `records` with the same `carry`. Jobs the request cites and the reading never names stay unchecked. This revision answers the five findings. External and std items no longer refuse (use-statement scope names, Cargo crate names, std/core/alloc/crate-name paths). The reading-named job is loaded. The 'new' marker window is a clause. The fixture readings of the whole crate run through the full chain. The decision entry states the departure from 'inside check_reading_acceptance'.

decisions.choice: Add a separate pub fn `check_named_dependencies` and chain it in `read_once` with `.and_then` after `check_reading_acceptance`. Its seams are the snapshot file set, the `earlier` jobs, the retried job id and a `symbol_found` closure. Extend the doc comment of `check_reading_acceptance` to say the repository-wide check follows it in `read_once`. The decision entry states plainly that the brief says 'via check_reading_acceptance' and that this plan chains instead, with the reason, so the verifier does not read it as a missed requirement (finding 5).
decisions.reason: `check_reading_acceptance` has about 45 call sites, nearly all tests passing None. Replay (`check_reading_text`) has no repository. A new function gives its own file-set, earlier-job and symbol seams without churn. Reader-level criterion 4 proves the wiring.

rejected.why: It changes about 45 call sites for no behavior gain, and replay would pass None.

rejected.option: Check in planner or critic prompts or at admission
rejected.why: Out of scope. The fault starts where unverified references are first admitted, which is the reading.

decisions.choice: Part 3 starts only from what the reading's own text names (title, summary, departures, assumptions, criteria; never out_of_scope). A job is relied on when the text names its id (case-insensitive). A file is relied on when the text names its full path, or its stem as a whole word. A stem counts only with at least 5 characters and a `_` or `-`. Naming the job id in out_of_scope exempts the whole job. The retried job triggers by path or stem only, never by its id. `earlier` = retried attempt + `referenced_jobs` (request citations) + jobs whose ids appear in the reading's own text, loaded through a new `named_earlier_jobs(records, reading, have, redactor)` that uses `job_ids_in` over `reading_text_fields` and `carry` (finding 2). A job loaded only because the reading names it is by construction relied on. The repair is a create deliverable or one out_of_scope entry naming it.
decisions.reason: Citing a job as evidence is not relying on it, and root-cause requests cite rejected jobs whose files never landed. The root cause is a named job's deliverable taken as existing, and the named job may be one the request never mentions, so the reading's own ids must be looked up too. The retried job's id appears in every retry reading, so an id trigger there would refuse every retry that drops a planned create. Its changed files are already handled by `unaccounted_files`.

rejected.option: Trigger on every job the request cites
rejected.why: Evidence-only citations would be refused, and the only repair would be boilerplate out_of_scope entries.

rejected.option: Only check jobs the request cites, and record the narrowing
rejected.why: This leaves the root cause's own case (a job named by the reading alone) unchecked; loading is cheap through the existing `carry`.

rejected.option: Decide 'did not land' from end_state or verdict
rejected.why: A rejected job's files can land through a later job; file presence in the snapshot is checkable.

decisions.choice: Part 2 checks symbols only in `Code survey:` assumptions (`code_surveys`). Path-like tokens (containing `/` or a dotted extension) are dropped first. A candidate is trimmed of punctuation and has at least 5 characters. Shapes: (a) snake_case containing `_`, bare or marked; (b) CamelCase with an internal lowercase-to-uppercase change, only with a code marker; (c) UPPER_SNAKE, only with a code marker. A code marker is a backtick span, a `::` path segment, or a directly following `(`. A `::` path is skipped whole when its first segment is `std`, `core`, `alloc`, `crate`, `self`, `super` or a Cargo crate name; its other segments are tested by the shapes. A symbol is exempt when a 'new' word (new, add, adds, added, adding, create, creates, created, creating, introduce, introduces, introducing) appears in the same clause before it: scanning back from the name to the previous `.`, `;`, `:` or newline, at most 8 words (finding 3). Tests cover 'adds a new pure function `x`'.
decisions.reason: GitHub and env-var names such as ATHENA_HOME are not candidates unless in code markup. Bare snake_case with an underscore is the common form of function names in surveys. A clause window covers 'adds a new pure function X', which the two-word window refused, and ends at a sentence boundary so a 'new' in an earlier sentence does not exempt a later symbol.

rejected.option: Two-word window for the new marker
rejected.why: Refuses 'adds a new pure function `x`', where the two preceding words are 'pure function'.

rejected.option: Accept any 5-character CamelCase or UPPER word
rejected.why: Brand names, emphasis words and environment-variable names would be refused, and the reader has one correction.

rejected.option: Check every identifier in every field
rejected.why: Names of things the change adds would refuse nearly every code reading.

decisions.choice: A symbol exists when the snapshot's .rs corpus defines it or brings it into scope, or it is a known crate name. (i) Definition: a line, after leading whitespace and qualifier words (pub, pub(crate), async, unsafe, const, extern), starting with fn/struct/enum/trait/union/type/const/static/mod/`macro_rules!` followed by the name as a whole word; a struct field line `name:`; an enum variant line. Lines starting `//` or a quote do not count. (ii) Scope: every identifier in a `use` statement (from `use` to the next `;`, across lines, with braces, `as` renames and globs) and every name in an `extern crate` line. So BTreeSet, HashMap, PathBuf and serde_json::Value pass because the workspace imports them (finding 1). (iii) Crate names: `[package] name` and every dependency key (`[dependencies]`, `[dev-dependencies]`, `[build-dependencies]`, `[workspace.dependencies]`, `[dependencies.x]`, including `x.workspace = true`) from every Cargo.toml in the snapshot, hyphens mapped to underscores, so `athena_core`, `serde_json` and `athena_core::reading::read_once` pass. Markdown and TOML text are excluded from (i) and (ii). `read_once` loads one batched `Git::cat_blobs` call over the .rs and Cargo.toml oids only when `survey_symbol_candidates` is non-empty. A pure `snapshot_corpus(entries, fetch)` returns the .rs text and the Cargo.toml text separately. A git error becomes `ReadError::Failed`. The check function stays infallible; `symbol_found` is `|s| corpus_has(&corpus, s)`.
decisions.reason: Surveys of this code routinely name std and external items that no workspace line defines. Counting what the workspace imports or declares as dependencies treats them as existing without a standard-library name list. Definition-only matching still keeps a comment, string or design doc from making a planned name exist. One batched call avoids a git process per file, and most readings load nothing.

rejected.option: Definitions only, as in the last plan
rejected.why: Refuses BTreeSet, HashMap, PathBuf, serde_json::Value and athena_core:: names, which are common in surveys of this code.

rejected.option: Narrow Part 2 to symbols that also appear in an earlier job's carried text
rejected.why: Misses the class where a reading invents a function with no job behind it; the import/crate rule fixes the false positives directly.

rejected.option: A hand-written list of std names
rejected.why: It goes stale and misses external crates; the workspace's own use lines and manifests are the measured source.
A comment or design doc would make the motivating name exist.

rejected.option: A lexer to strip comments and strings
rejected.why: Raw strings and nested comments need a real lexer; the line-start match covers the cases that matter.

decisions.choice: An unfound item (path, symbol or unlanded file) is accounted for by a Create deliverable (the path, a directory above it, or for a symbol a path component or file stem of one), or by an out_of_scope item naming it as a whole token via `names_path_token`. A Modify or Delete of a missing path does not account for it. A shared helper is extracted from `unaccounted_files`, whose behavior and tests do not change.
decisions.reason: This is the reading's own rule: list the item as a deliverable to create, or put it in out_of_scope. It reuses the existing token matcher.

rejected.why: That is the failure: prose that assumes existence.

decisions.choice: Part 1 path tokens: split text on whitespace and quote or bracket characters, trim trailing punctuation and `:NNN`, and keep tokens containing `/` whose first component is a top-level directory of `files`, with a short alphabetic extension and no glob, placeholder or brace characters. A crate-relative path such as `src/reading.rs` is unchecked. The narrowing is recorded in D146 and in the doc comment, and a test shows a missing `src/missing.rs` passes.
decisions.reason: Resolving by suffix would guess which file is meant and could refuse truthful surveys. Recording the narrowing is cheaper and honest.

rejected.option: Resolve `src/x.rs` when exactly one snapshot path ends with it
rejected.why: A missing crate-relative file would still pass, and the rule adds code for a narrow case.

decisions.choice: The check runs only when `files` is Some, the reading has a capability and no open question. Replay does not run it. The 8% is a declared expectation (replay_declaration share 8), not measured. No stored past readings exist in the snapshot (records/ is absent; Glob found no reading files), so Criterion 6 is shown by a table over hand-built readings plus every fixture reading that already passes through `read_once` in run_pin_tests.rs and run/tests.rs when the whole crate runs. CHANGELOG.md and D146 say that no stored corpus was available and that the table is not a replay (finding 4).
decisions.reason: It has the same guard as `check_boundary_and_repo_files`. Replay has no repository or earlier jobs. Fixture readings in the existing tests are the only real reading-shaped data the repository holds, and they already run the full chain once step 5 is wired.

rejected.option: Run in replay with an invented file set
Present the table as a replay
rejected.why: It is hand-built; claiming a measurement would mislead the verifier.

decisions.choice: Add run_pin_tests.rs as a deliverable with reader-level tests through `Athena::ask`, next to the test near line 1707, using `repo`, `config`, `athena_with`, `reader_edits` and `refusal_section`.
decisions.reason: Pure-function tests pass even if `read_once` never calls the check. The fake-reader tests run `ask` through `read_for`, `read_once`, `ls_tree` and `cat_blobs`.

rejected.why: The fix could go unwired with every test green.

risks.risk: False refusals: a survey or summary names a new file or function as part of the change.
risks.mitigation: The error says to list it as a create deliverable, name it in out_of_scope, write 'new' or 'adds' earlier in the clause before a survey symbol, or drop it. Globs, placeholders, braces, extensionless tokens, crate-relative paths and non-snapshot first components are ignored. Each guard has a test.

risks.risk: Standard-library, external-crate or workspace-crate names in a survey (BTreeSet, serde_json::Value, athena_core::...) are refused because no workspace line defines them, using up the reader's one correction.
risks.mitigation: A name counts when any `use` statement or `extern crate` line in the .rs corpus mentions it, or it is a crate name from the Cargo.toml files, or its path starts with std, core, alloc, crate, self, super or a crate name. Guard tests cover BTreeSet, serde_json::Value, athena_core:: and PathBuf.

risks.risk: Brand words, environment-variable names and local bindings in a survey are taken for symbols.
risks.mitigation: CamelCase and UPPER_SNAKE need a code marker; path-like tokens are dropped first; at least 5 characters. Guard tests cover GitHub and ATHENA_HOME. Bare snake_case such as a `let` binding can still be refused; the message offers out_of_scope or a 'new' marker.

risks.risk: A job named in the reading's prose as evidence now forces an entry, including jobs the request never cites.
risks.mitigation: Only an id, path or stem named outside out_of_scope triggers, never a request citation alone. The repair is one out_of_scope entry naming the job id, stated in the error. Tests show the six unnamed cited jobs are unchecked.

risks.risk: The new loading of reading-named jobs reads records for ids the reader invented or mistyped.
risks.mitigation: `records.jobs.get` ignores unknown ids, as `referenced_jobs` does; an unknown id adds nothing to `earlier`. A unit test covers an unknown id.

risks.risk: A comment, string or fixture holding a name counts as existence.
risks.mitigation: The match is definition-only plus use-statement names: line-start items, fields and variants; comment, doc and quoted lines are skipped. A definition inside a #[cfg(test)] module still counts (known small gap). Test fixtures build names from pieces.

risks.risk: Existing `read_once`-level fixtures in run_pin_tests.rs or run/tests.rs name prose paths absent from their snapshot and now fail.
risks.mitigation: Run `cargo test -p athena-core` early. Fix a fixture only where it names an absent path; never weaken the check.

risks.risk: Replay cannot see the new refusals, and no stored past readings exist, so the 8% is not measured and the table could be mistaken for a replay.
risks.mitigation: Declare the expectation in the criteria; state in D146, CHANGELOG and the test comment that it is unmeasured and that the table is not a replay; run all fixture readings through the full chain via the whole crate's tests.

risks.risk: Corpus load cost or a git error.
risks.mitigation: Load only when a survey names a candidate symbol, once, over .rs and Cargo.toml entries only. A git error is `ReadError::Failed`, not a refusal.

risks.risk: The boundary scan or personal-data allow-list trips on new text.
risks.mitigation: Keep docs and tests free of banned words and email-like text; build odd strings from pieces. Run the boundary and budgets tests in `cargo test --locked`.

demonstrations.method: Unit test `a_reading_relying_on_an_unlanded_earlier_job_is_refused_unless_accounted_for` in the reading.rs test module. It runs the production chain `check_reading_acceptance(&reading, request, None, &referenced, Some(&files))` then `check_named_dependencies(&reading, &files, &earlier, retried, &symbol_found)`. Preconditions: capability set, no open question, files Some. Fixture file set: `files_at_head()` plus a few paths. Reading built with the existing `code_reading` or `governed_reading`. `earlier` holds an `EarlierAttempt` built like the existing `earlier()` helper (line 5813) with `changed_files: ["added crates/athena-core/src/code_health.rs"]` and `reading_deliverables: ["create crates/athena-context/prompts/context-engineer.md"]`. Everything is injected as arguments. The function is added by step 4; the helpers exist today. Cases: the summary names the job id as something it builds on; the chain is Err containing 'was refused', the job id and both paths, while `check_reading_acceptance` alone is Ok. A reading naming only a file path (no id) is refused naming the job's file. Ok when the file is a Create deliverable, when out_of_scope names the path or the job id, and when the fixture file set holds the file. A Modify of the missing path is still refused.
demonstrations.observes: Err with 'was refused', the job id and the missing files for the unaccounted cases; Ok for create, out_of_scope and present-in-snapshot cases.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without `check_named_dependencies` the test does not compile; a stub returning Ok(()) fails the refusal asserts; without the Part 3 id/path trigger the named-job case is accepted; without the accounting rule the create and out_of_scope cases are refused wrongly.

demonstrations.method: Table-driven unit test `the_dependency_check_covers_paths_symbols_roles_and_job_files_not_one_job` calling the production `check_named_dependencies`. File set, `earlier` slice and a symbol closure over the production `corpus_has(fixture_corpus, s)` are injected arguments (added by steps 3 and 4). Symbol fixture names are built with `concat()`. Cases: (a) a missing path in the summary, `crates/athena-core/src/code_health.rs`; (b) a role prompt path `crates/athena-context/prompts/context-engineer.md`, where the reading names only the stem `context-engineer` and the file is in an earlier job's unlanded creates; (c) a `Code survey:` symbol with no definition in the corpus; (d) symbols defined by an `fn` line, a struct field line and an enum variant line pass; (e) a symbol held only in a `//` comment, a `///` doc line, a quoted string or a markdown-style line is refused (a `defines_symbol` table). Also: `snapshot_corpus` over entries with a .md, a .toml and a Cargo.toml keeps only .rs text for definitions (and Cargo.toml text for crate names), through an injected fetch closure; 'adds X beside Y' passes X and refuses an absent Y; 'adds a new pure function `X`' passes X (clause window); each refused case is accepted once the item is a Create deliverable or in out_of_scope.
demonstrations.observes: At least four distinct kinds are refused separately (path, role path via stem, symbol, comment-only symbol); each error names its own item; each is accepted once accounted for; the corpus keeps only .rs for definitions.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without Part 1, (a) fails; without the stem trigger, (b) fails; without the symbol part, (c) fails; a bare word-match corpus fails (e) and the corpus test; a check keyed to one job's file name fails the other cases; a two-word 'new' window fails the 'adds a new pure function' case.

demonstrations.method: Unit test `jobs_the_request_cites_as_evidence_are_unchecked_when_the_reading_never_names_them` calling `check_reading_acceptance` and `check_named_dependencies`. `earlier` holds six `EarlierAttempt` values built like `earlier()` (ids 20261025-001236-brde, 20261026-145124-ssmw, 20261026-145955-s7e2, 20261026-042558-5p65, 20261026-064950-38jx, 20261026-065228-02zf), each with an unlanded added file or create deliverable (code_health.rs, steward.rs, status.rs, gh.rs and so on) absent from the file set. The reading uses this request's own wording and fields: title, summary, the brief's assumptions, the three out-of-scope items and the eight criteria. It names only the retried job 20261030-060751-5389, whose carried files are existing modify paths. Expect Ok. Variants: the same reading with the summary naming one cited job's id is refused naming that job's files; a retried job with a planned create absent from the snapshot and its id named is still Ok, but naming its stem is refused. Seam: function arguments; exists after step 4.
demonstrations.observes: Ok for the evidence-only citations and the self-application reading; Err only when the reading's own text names a cited job, one of its files, or a file stem.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests `guard_words_and_crate_relative_paths_are_not_refused` and `external_and_std_names_in_a_survey_are_not_refused`, calling the production `survey_symbol_candidates` and `check_named_dependencies` with `Code survey:` assumptions and a corpus from the production `snapshot_corpus`. Guard cases: a survey mentioning GitHub and ATHENA_HOME bare gives no candidates and is Ok with an empty corpus; the same names in backticks are candidates and refused when undefined and not imported (the marker rule is pinned both ways, and the test comment says so); a bare `let` binding such as repo_files is a candidate and refused when undefined (documents the limit). External cases with a corpus holding `use std::collections::{BTreeSet, HashMap};` and a Cargo.toml with `serde_json` in dependencies and package name `athena-core`: `BTreeSet`, `serde_json::Value`, `athena_core::reading::read_once` and `std::path::PathBuf` in backticks are Ok, and a marked name with no import, definition or crate is refused. Crate-relative: a prose path `src/missing.rs` in the summary is Ok, with a test comment (and a D146 sentence) saying it is unchecked. Globs, `<name>` placeholders, a non-snapshot first component, all-caps words (NEVER, HTTPS) and plain lowercase words give no refusal. Seam: function arguments; added by steps 3 and 4.
demonstrations.observes: No refusal for the bare GitHub and ATHENA_HOME survey, for imported or crate-named items, or for the crate-relative missing path; the marked, undefined forms are refused.
demonstrations.fails_without: If CamelCase and UPPER_SNAKE need no marker, the bare guard survey is refused; if `use` names and crate names are not honoured, the BTreeSet and serde_json cases are refused; if the path rule resolved crate-relative paths, the `src/missing.rs` case is refused.

demonstrations.method: Test `the_missing_dependency_refusal_is_a_declared_higher_refusal_rate`: `replay_declaration(&criteria, &[])` (line 3299) on the criterion 'expected 8% of newly refused readings' gives `share == Some(8)` and `unsupported_share() == None`. Test `readings_that_rely_on_nothing_from_a_cited_job_pass_the_full_chain` runs a table through `check_reading_acceptance` then `check_named_dependencies`: a first attempt, a code reading with existing paths and defined or imported survey symbols, a reading with evidence-only cited jobs holding unlanded files, a decline, a question, and this request's self-application reading. Each is Ok. A further test passes every reading the existing reading.rs fixture helpers build (`governed_reading`, `code_reading` and the like) through the full chain. The comment and the CHANGELOG/D146 text say that no stored past readings exist in the snapshot (records/ absent) and that replay passes no repository, so the table is not a replay and the 8% stays a declared, unmeasured expectation. The fixture readings in run_pin_tests.rs and run/tests.rs go through `read_once` with the chain wired, so the full `cargo test -p athena-core` shows none is newly refused. Fixtures that name an absent path are fixed only where wrong.
demonstrations.observes: share is 8; every table reading and every fixture reading passes; the unaccounted cases of criteria 1 to 3 are refused, so accepted-before and refused-after are both shown.
demonstrations.fails_without: A check that over-refuses fails the table and the fixtures; a check that refuses nothing fails criteria 1 and 2; a malformed declaration makes `share` None.

demonstrations.method: Content check by Grep (the verifier may use the Grep tool for the same pattern and Read the new entries). demonstrations.observes: One matching line in each of the three files, plus each narrowing named in the decision record.

demonstrations.method: Run the three checks Athena runs, from the repository root. They cover all new tests, the existing `read_once`-level fixtures, the budgets test (no prompt changes, so no budget moves) and the boundary scan on the new text.
demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked
demonstrations.fails_without: A missing or uncompilable check fails to build; unformatted code fails fmt; an unused helper or needless clone fails clippy under -D warnings; a fixture reading naming an absent path fails until fixed.
